questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The culture, the language and the academic heritage.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy, the website and course catalogue was just a pile of PDF documents some of them outdated.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good assistance everyone was nice to answer my emails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Cité Universitaire, not exactly on campus but sort of.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a place to buy cheap meals everyday (Crous), but cooking facilities were horrible.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Big differences between different houses in the Cité Universitaire, and that it is a bit of a social bubble.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
An obsolete method, even had to register physically for one course. There was no central system but a lot of different analogue systems. Had to write a bunch of emails. 

Should not be that difficult for such a big university to create a simple integrated online system.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Find the course catalogue in a pile of PDF documents from last year, with little to no information. Write to professors if they accepted Erasmus students. Then write another email to an administrativ worker, who would write me on the list. For the other course i had to show up physically at a specific location, so that an administrativ worker could write some things on his computer and print a piece of paper that he handed to me.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The co-ordinators were nice to answer all my emails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I succeeded.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's chaos, but don't worry, it's the same for everybody. The approach is more loose than in Denmark, so you figure things out along the way.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Low academic level. There was not much involvement of academic papers. 

The presentations of the professors were unstructured and superficial.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Very different. Some courses it was a two hour monologue from a professor without a plan or anything visual. 
They are way more concerned with historical facts and not as much with methodology or theory.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
New Perspectives in Religious Studies
The Story of Brexit - From Entry to th 2016 Referendum
Contemporary British Drama: What is political theatre?
Histoire de relations internationales  - L'OTAN Depuis le Guerre Froide

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The Story of Brexit - From Entry to th 2016 Referendum
Histoire de relations internationales  - L'OTAN Depuis le Guerre Froide 

The professors were nice and the subject interesting. Teaching methods and academic level however were limited.

questions.answer: Food was more expensive than expected.

questions.answer: Rent of a bike was cheap as well as public transport.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think a lot, but because i was enrolled at the Cité Universitaire, i used the activities there.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Football. It is just an international language that breaks down barriers and offers you to meet new people in an informal way.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hang out with friends, go to sports events, visit other towns in the area, and maybe to go a market by some nice food and cook a big meal together on Sundays.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy, the place i lived was also very international. However, had to get used to living in a city that big (Paris).

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really. Didn't interact much with them, but maybe ask them out. Go watch a football match together or somethin like that.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People ignore each other a lot in Paris, which i had to get used to. Starting the day later and eating later was also hard for me to adapt to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The aesthetic aspirations, and the romantic lifestyle that still thrives in the country.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't worry too much. Things are more loose and you will figure things out along the way.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write emails that is your best weapon. Talk to the other students to make calm yourself.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people from all around the world that was an amazing experience. Really gaining new perspectives on the world and myself through discussions with other people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adapting to a different mindset. Accepting that you cannot control what is going on. The uncertainty about demands, rules and norms, that was difficult to cope with.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
